scope_summary: Application state under real interaction sequences on the audited build (md5 f10fe585c46aea576f436ed51ac46f83, 2,810,630 bytes) in the pinned Chromium 141 on SwiftShader: 14 scenario scripts (s1-s14, with re-checks s1b, s10b, s11b) driving visitor pages at 1600x900, 1280x720 and 880x660 (density 2), a touchscreen-laptop page and phone pages (390x844, density 3, touch) by real mouse, wheel, keys, taps and CDP touch, the app's own frame loop stepped on a 30 fps clock by the frame driver (ilib.js DRV). Covered: seeks while playing with the dwell on and off, speed changes in Play and in each stage of a dwell, presentation/ground/relief changes during Play, selection and Follow across phases and under a reading, panels while dragging, revisiting a clock by different paths, the opening/tour interrupted and the reset paths, resize 1600-1024-700-390 and a phone turned with panels open, Play to the end, rapid input, listener/timer/GPU growth over two rounds of cycles, and the area 'state' browser hypotheses (findings 1-4, 6-8). Eight findings (one S2, four S3, three S4); seven of the state area's eight findings confirmed in the browser; no console warning or error in any run.

findings.title: A pan, zoom or keyboard pan during a camera glide is undone: the glide carries the camera on to its destination
findings.user_impact: After clicking a vantage, an order-of-battle row or a formation (the centring glide, 1.5 s), a phase (2.6 s), a theme or a tour stop, a visitor who starts dragging, zooming or panning by keys before the glide ends sees the move fought and then reverted: the camera finishes at the glide's view while the Follow button shows off.
refs: app.js:6854-6905 (bindCanvas: pointer, touch and wheel handlers)
app.js:2548 (redrawGround stops both slots since 8H: the one input that does)
docs/STAGE3_SPEC.md:249-252 ('off, the eye stays where the visitor put it')
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s14-glide-input.json: 10 frames into each glide, real input, then 90 frames: vantage (Zuran) + drag: camera moved 525.5 (target+eye displacement, units) after the release to the preset; vantage (Pratzen) + wheel x3: 185.7; dossier centring (Legrand's OOB row) + drag: 185.9; vantage (Allied) + map arrow keys x5: 335.4; freeCam true and the camera slot running at release in each. docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s10-phone.json phone-drag-follow + docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s10b-phone-drag.json: a finger pan 2-2.5 s after tapping phase 4 in the phone's list ended at that phase's preset target (7,10,12) = PHASES[4].cam (7,8,12) framed to the ground; with no glide running the pan holds (3/3).
findings.expected: Any pan, orbit, zoom or key pan stops the running glide where it is; the eye stays where the visitor left it (Stage 3 spec, A.3).
findings.observed: Follow turns off but the camera slot keeps running and overwrites the camera every frame until the glide's end.
findings.remedy: Stop the camera slot when the visitor takes the camera: in LANDCAM.free() (and the paper map's MAPCAM moves) call setTween('cam',null) and clear camArc, as redrawGround does since 8H; add a self-test check (drag, wheel, keys during each kind of glide leave the camera where the input left it) and a css-test rule.
findings.validation: re-run s14 and s10/s10b: moved after input < 0.05
findings.cause_verified: yes (code read; the camera slot is set at release in every case)

findings.title: The timeline's tooltip covers the control row and swallows a press on Play reached from the timeline
findings.user_impact: Hovering an event marker, a phase or an act shows its tip above it, over Play, Next, Next event and Follow; it stays while the pointer is over it (WCAG 1.4.13), so moving straight up from the timeline to Play lands on the tip and the first press does nothing (it only dismisses the tip).
refs: app.js:7439-7445 (tipShow: placed at r.top-h-8, above the hovered element)
app.js:7457-7476 (bindTimeTips: the tip hoverable, pointerover clears its hide)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s13-tip-covers.json: at 1280x720 the 07:00 marker's tip box [92,641,472,688] overlaps prev, play, next, nextEv, follow and the act/phase buttons; the centres of Play, Next, Next event, Follow covered; pointer moved from the marker to Play in 12 steps and pressed: element under the pointer #tltip, playing false before and after; at 1600x900 the same (the tips of the phase/act buttons crossed on the way cover Play). Control: pointer to empty ground for 300 ms first, then Play toggles (both sizes). Found by docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s5-revisit-determinism.run1.json (path F: '#play is covered by #tltip').
findings.expected: A tip never covers the controls a visitor reaches for from the timeline, or a press on a control under it reaches the control.
findings.observed: The press goes to the tip; Play does not toggle.
findings.remedy: Place the tips where they cannot cover the timebar's control row (above the timebar or beside the element), or give the control row precedence (the tip yields when the pointer enters a control's box), keeping 1.4.13's hoverability; add a check to the tips self-test.

findings.title: At an event start the event marker's hit area covers the time rail's playhead: a drag that starts on the playhead does not scrub
findings.user_impact: The playhead sits on a marker at 04:00, at every dwell's hold and after every event jump; pressing it to drag the clock presses the marker instead (a drag does nothing, a click opens the event's dossier). Elsewhere the rail works.
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s1b-recheck.json: rail centre line at 1600 px: 356 of 1,570 px (22.7%) hit an event marker (25 markers); at 04:00 the playhead's centre hits the 04:00 marker; in the 04:15 hold it hits button.ev-mark.al.on.dw, and a 200 px drag from it left the clock at 04:15 (playing on). The first run's rail drag at 08:00 fell on a marker the same way (docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s1-seek-dwell-speed.json drag-while-playing).
findings.expected: A press-and-drag starting on the playhead scrubs the clock.
findings.observed: The marker takes the press; the rail never sees it.
findings.remedy: Let a press that starts on a marker and moves past a few pixels scrub the rail (select the event only on a click without movement), or keep the markers' enlarged hit area off the rail's lower half, or give the playhead its own handle above the markers.

findings.title: With the Movement layer off, every phase change flashes the outgoing phase's arrows at 0.87 opacity
findings.user_impact: A visitor who turned the arrows off sees the previous phase's arrows appear and fade over about 1.1 s at each phase change (PageDown, a phase button, a boundary during Play).
refs: app.js:3180-3186 (applyOverlayOpacity: the current group times base=layerOn.arrows?0.95:0, the outgoing group 0.9*ovFadeOut without it)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s11b-arrows-tier.json: Movement off at 08:00 (current group opacity 0); PageDown to 08:45: the 08:00 group's 41 materials at 0.873 on the first frame, then 0.845, 0.735, 0.625 ... 28 of 40 frames above 0.1, the outgoing group visible; drawn frames s11b-arrows-tier-arrows-off-0800.jpg, -arrows-off-pagedown-0845.jpg.
findings.expected: With the layer off no arrow is drawn, the outgoing phase's included.
findings.observed: The outgoing group is drawn at 0.9 x its fade.
findings.remedy: Multiply the outgoing group's opacity by the same layer factor as the current group (one expression in applyOverlayOpacity); add a self-test check.
findings.dependencies: related to area 'state' finding 3 (the outgoing group reset to 0.9 when a fade is interrupted)

findings.title: Under a reading that does not know a formation, its card's 'Doing now' still names where it is
findings.user_impact: The card says 'Where: Not known to Allied headquarters at 07:30' and, two rows above, 'Doing now: Standing in fog behind Puntowitz, hidden from the plateau'; the reading's hiding of the formation's place is undone in prose.
refs: app.js:7818 (the 'Doing now' row, not tested against readHidden)
docs/STAGE8_SPEC.md:1671-1686 (13.1: hidden 'from every place a visitor could read its position from'; act texts 'reviewed and kept ... orders, not places')
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s3-selection-reading.json reading0730.card and docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s11-state-hypotheses-card-under-allied-reading-0730-dom.jpg (real clicks: OOB row, the Eyes button twice). Scope (docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s12-act-leak.json, app globals, every 10 min): Napoleon's reading hides a formation with a 'Doing now' text 480 formation-clocks, 320 of them naming a place (18 distinct texts, e.g. Kienmayer 07:00-12:40 'Attacks Telnitz'); the Allied reading 798, 304 naming a place (17 texts).
findings.expected: Decision 251 as 8A records it: a formation the reading does not know is hidden from every place a visitor could read its position from.
findings.observed: 8A kept act texts as 'orders, not places', but these texts state places and present activity.
findings.remedy: Owner decision: under a reading, give an unknown formation's 'Doing now' and 'From HH:MM' rows the place rows' 'Not known to ... at ...' (or keep them with a note that the text is the visitor's, not the headquarters'); extend runtime-test's decision-251 block.

findings.title: Pausing in a dwell's hold leaves the caption naming the dwell's events; the same clock reached by a seek names one
findings.user_impact: At 07:00 paused in the dwell the caption reads '... leave the plateau; Kienmayer attacks Telnitz', after a seek to 07:00 only '... leave the plateau' (both true); it changes at the next clock change.
refs: app.js:7352-7377 (paintSituation: its key holds playing and the dwell's events)
findings.expected: The caption is a function of the state it keys on.
findings.observed: Stale until the next clock change.
findings.remedy: Call paintSituation() from stopPlay (and dwellReset), or decide that the dwell's caption should persist at a paused event start and key it so.

findings.title: A modal sheet opened mid-drag does not end the drag: the map pans under the '?' sheet
findings.user_impact: With the mouse button held on the map, '?' opens the keys sheet while the map keeps panning behind it until release.
refs: app.js:6854-6894 (bindCanvas: pointer capture, the drag ends only at pointerup/pointercancel)
findings.evidence: docs/audit-post8-evidence/interaction/s6-panels-while-dragging.json help-mid-drag: target x -60.8 to -82.8 (22 units for 60 px) while the sheet was open; no drag held after release.
findings.expected: Opening a modal dialog ends any drag in progress.
findings.observed: The captured drag continues under the dialog.
findings.remedy: End the canvas drag (panEnd, drag=null, release capture) when a sheet opens.

findings.title: Focus falls to the page when a resize hides the focused control
findings.user_impact: A keyboard user with focus on Layers who narrows the window below 720 px (the tools go behind the Menu) is left on the body, and stays there when the window widens again.
refs: app.js:7189-7203 (shown/focusTo: used when panels close, SW-5)
findings.expected: SW-5's rule: focus handed to a shown successor.
findings.observed: Focus on body after the resize.
findings.remedy: In onResize, if the focused element is no longer shown, focusTo a successor (the Menu button on the phone layout, else Play).

scope of IA-5 (app globals on a harness page)
2 of 4 not as expected (IA-2); controls as expected
4 of 4 exercised cases not as expected (IA-1); the phase-glide case not exercised

experiments.limitations: environment only; the scenario scripts finish CSS transitions as a set-up where they click inside a sliding panel

not_checked: Real hardware and real-time behaviour: every run used the frame driver's 30 fps clock under SwiftShader; wall-clock figures here are not device timings.

The native context menu (headless shows none): the right-button path of state finding 7 is confirmed up to the seek and the unprevented contextmenu event; that the menu swallows the release is inferred.
State finding 5 (the reading cached at the first instant of a minute) in the browser: not re-tested (node-confirmed by the state area).
A drag during a phase glide on the desktop (s14's case ran with Follow already off); the phone's equivalent is confirmed.
Reduced motion during these sequences; Firefox and WebKit engines; screen readers; pinch during a glide; sessions longer than two rounds of cycles.
CSS-transition timing as a visitor sees it (transitions were finished as a set-up where needed: an environment workaround, recorded).
strengths: Every seek during Play stops it and lands exactly; Play resumes forward with the next dwell ahead; no backward step in any trace.
The dwell's toggle (S-2) and 8H's speed changes inside a dwell behave in the browser exactly as the node checks predict (hold 1.5 s kept, the new rate exact).
Presentation, ground and relief changes during Play are consistent; a relief change mid-glide stops both tween slots (8H S-7).
Opening and tour: every interruption ends in its documented state; the reset paths return to a fresh page's state.
Seeks are deterministic: 07:00 by four different paths and 09:20 from both sides give identical frame states; the same 14-step sequence twice is identical.
No listener, timer, observer, GPU or DOM growth in a second round of cycles; no console warning or error in any of the 20 recorded runs.
